whatItIs.text: Churned cream — about 81% butterfat — used as a spread, a cooking fat, and the backbone of baking.

historyNote.text: Butter has been churned since antiquity, and salt was added from the start to keep it from spoiling on journeys; the word itself may come from Greek boutyron, cow-cheese.

howToChoose.text: Check the date and take blocks from the back of the chiller where it is colder; foil wraps protect best against fridge odours.

storage.text: Refrigerate what you will use this week; extra blocks freeze well. The rulebook has the storage-window details.

foodSafetyRef.note: storage windows live in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Brown it for nutty sauces, whip softened butter with herbs for a topping, or freeze in spoonfuls for later baking.

substitutions.note: for dairy-free cooking and bakes; slightly denser, less crisp results
